final.memo:
Ligand Pharmaceuticals is a textbook example of a company with valuable underlying pharmaceutical assets whose market price has been decimated by a management-induced governance and accounting failure. While the stock currently languishes due to its September 7th Nasdaq delisting and ongoing financial restatements, we believe the enterprise is significantly mispriced [D01, D03].

When viewed on a sum-of-the-parts basis, the value of Ligand's marketed products and scientific IP portfolio far exceeds the current enterprise value of $843.9 million [D01, D04]. The company's current financial performance is abysmal, posting a 2004 EBIT margin of -22.9% against a benchmark of 38.9% at peers like Amgen, representing a clear operational failure that we intend to rectify [D06].

Market participants are currently panic-selling, blinded by the uncertainty of the delisting and the restatement of 2002-2004 financials [D02, D07]. We see this as an opportunity; the core business remains intact, and the current governance discount is a direct consequence of board incompetence that can be corrected through aggressive shareholder activism [D03].

Our plan is clear: we will initiate a 13D filing to demand the immediate appointment of an independent forensic audit committee and the replacement of the current board [D03]. We expect to utilize the upcoming annual meeting nomination window to ensure leadership that is focused on operational restructuring, margin improvement, and relisting compliance within the next two quarters [D03, D06].

While we acknowledge the risks inherent in a delisted security, the downside is protected by a cash-heavy balance sheet that provides a floor of roughly $4.50 per share [D04]. Our conviction is high that with proper governance and accountability, we can see significant upside toward our $18.00 target [D04].

We are initiating a 5% position in the common stock, sized above our typical entry due to the strength of the underlying asset floor and the clear catalyst for governance intervention. We will hedge our exposure with index futures to neutralize sector beta while we execute our plan [D03, D05].
